metadata.value: Map of Italy from Ptolemy's Cosmographia (Ulm, 1482)

metadata.label: Format
metadata.value: 1 map : woodcut, hand color ; 35 x 54 cm

metadata.label: Description
metadata.value: The woodcuts in the Ulm Ptolemy are generally credited to Johannes 'Schnitzer' ("the woodblock-cutter") from Armsheim.  One characteristic of his work is that he tended to reverse his capital 'N's when cutting the letter. Of the Italian editions of Ptolemy only one, that of Bernard Sylvanus, published in Venice in 1511, used woodcuts.  All the others used copper engravings.

metadata.label: Note
metadata.value: The first century of United States political parties is illustrated with a river metaphor. Color helps distinguish each party. Flow widths display relative party strength, with leading parties on top. Offshoots spring from the main flows into splinter parties. The decades leading up to the Civil War evoke writhing snakes. Annotations abound, noting historic events and legislative accomplishments, but they never distract from the colorful flows. A parallel congressional timeline, on the bottom, uses the same color palette to indicate which party has power over each house. The upper chamber of the Senate is on top. The head of state occupies the highest row of the composition.

metadata.label: Pub Title
metadata.value: Conspectus of The History of Political Parties and the Federal Government.

metadata.label: Pub Reference
metadata.value: For full text scans of this book see https://archive.org/details/conspectusofhist00houg

metadata.label: Pub Note
metadata.value: Colorful maps, charts, and timelines recount the political history of the first one hundred years of the United States. One iconic timeline shows the flow of political party power. Another timeline details each presidential administration. Includes an update to an 1874 fiscal chart originally by Francis Amasa Walker - see atlas plate XXXVa https://www.davidrumsey.com/luna/servlet/s/yj1uv3

metadata.label: Title
metadata.value: Map of Greenwich Village made for the Whitney Studio Club. W.E. Rudge

metadata.label: Description
metadata.value: Bright color bird's eye view pictorial map of Greenwich Village in the 1920s, copyright at lower left: W.E. Rudge. Showing the village through the puffy clouds which are the link to the uncolored pictorial border. Shows detailed view of the buildings, streets, parks, ships, mermaid and sea monster. Includes 2 quotes by John Reed in the puffy clouds at upper left and right. Around the cartouche are winged faces, apparently portraits of the artists. Unusual and rare pictorial map of Greenwich Village.
